slides.title: Welcome to Our Surroundings
slides.content:
# Our Surroundings - The World Around Us!

Everything you see, hear, feel, and experience around you is part of your **surroundings**.

## What You Will Learn:
- Your **home and school** environment
- **Natural surroundings** vs **man-made surroundings**
- **Community spaces** and their importance
- How to be **aware** of and protect our environment

## What Are Surroundings?
- Surroundings are everything around us
- They include both **living** and **non-living** things
- Our surroundings affect how we **feel** and **live**

## Examples of Surroundings:
- The **trees, plants, and animals** around you
- The **buildings, roads, and parks** in your area
- The **air, water, and soil** around you
- The **people** in your family and community

> **Look Around:** Take a moment right now. What do you see around you? Those things are your surroundings!

slides.title: Home Environment
slides.content:
# Your Home Environment

Your **home** is the most important part of your surroundings. It is where you live, play, eat, and sleep.

## Parts of a Home:

### Indoor Spaces:
- **Bedroom** - where you sleep and rest
- **Kitchen** - where food is prepared
- **Bathroom** - for bathing and hygiene
- **Living room** - for family time and relaxation
- **Study area** - where you do homework

### Outdoor Spaces:
- **Garden/Yard** - for playing and growing plants
- **Balcony/Terrace** - open space for fresh air
- **Garage** - for parking vehicles

## Keeping Your Home Clean:
- Pick up your **toys and belongings** after use
- Put **garbage** in the dustbin, not on the floor
- Help **dust** and **sweep** your room
- Keep your study desk **organized**
- Open **windows** for fresh air and sunlight

## Why a Clean Home Matters:
- Clean homes have **fewer germs** and diseases
- A tidy room helps you **concentrate** better
- Fresh air and sunlight keep your home **healthy**
- It makes your home a **happy place** to live

## Things That Make a Good Home:
- Clean **water** for drinking and washing
- **Electricity** for lights and appliances
- Proper **ventilation** (airflow)
- **Safety** features (locks, fire safety)
- **Love and care** from family!

> **Your Job:** Even young children can help keep their home clean. Start by making your bed and putting things back in their place!

slides.title: School Environment
slides.content:
# Your School Environment

School is your second home! You spend many hours there learning and making friends.

## Parts of a School:

### Indoor Spaces:
- **Classrooms** - where you learn and study
- **Library** - full of books and knowledge
- **Lab/Science room** - for experiments
- **Computer room** - for learning technology
- **Canteen** - for eating meals
- **Principal's office** - school administration

### Outdoor Spaces:
- **Playground** - for sports and games
- **Garden** - flowers and plants
- **Assembly area** - for morning gatherings
- **Parking area** - for vehicles

## Keeping School Clean:

### Your Responsibilities:
- Do not **litter** in classrooms or playground
- Use **dustbins** for waste
- Keep your **desk and bag** organized
- Do not write on **walls or desks**
- Clean up after eating your **lunch**

### School Responsibilities:
- Regular **cleaning** of rooms and toilets
- Clean **drinking water** for students
- Proper **waste disposal**
- Maintaining **gardens** and green areas

## What Makes a Good School Environment:

| Feature | Why It Matters |
|---------|---------------|
| Clean classrooms | Better learning |
| Green playground | Fresh air and exercise |
| Clean toilets | Health and hygiene |
| Clean drinking water | Prevents diseases |
| Proper lighting | Protects eyesight |

> **Be Responsible:** Your school belongs to everyone. Take care of it as you would take care of your own home!

slides.title: Natural Surroundings
slides.content:
# Natural Surroundings

**Natural surroundings** are things found in nature that were NOT made by humans.

## Examples of Natural Surroundings:

### Living Natural Things:
- **Trees and plants** - forests, gardens, grasslands
- **Animals** - birds, insects, fish, mammals
- **Tiny organisms** - bacteria, algae

### Non-living Natural Things:
- **Water** - rivers, lakes, oceans, rain
- **Air** - the atmosphere around us
- **Soil** - the ground beneath our feet
- **Rocks and mountains** - landforms
- **Sunlight** - energy from the sun

## Types of Natural Surroundings:

| Type | What You Find There |
|------|---------------------|
| Forests | Trees, animals, birds, streams |
| Rivers and lakes | Fish, water plants, frogs |
| Mountains | Snow, rocks, mountain animals |
| Deserts | Sand, cacti, camels, lizards |
| Oceans | Marine life, coral, waves |
| Grasslands | Open fields, grazing animals |

## Why Natural Surroundings Are Important:
- They provide **oxygen** for breathing
- They give us **food** and **water**
- They are home to **millions of species**
- They give us **wood, medicines, and materials**
- They make our world **beautiful**
- They help control **climate and weather**

## The Balance of Nature:
- Every part of nature is **connected**
- Plants, animals, water, and air all work **together**
- When one part is damaged, everything is affected

> **Nature is Not a Place to Visit - It is Home!** We are all part of nature, and protecting it means protecting ourselves.

slides.title: Man-made Surroundings
slides.content:
# Man-made Surroundings

**Man-made surroundings** are things created by humans. They are built to make our lives easier and more comfortable.

## Examples of Man-made Surroundings:

### Buildings and Structures:
- **Houses and apartments** - where we live
- **Schools and colleges** - where we learn
- **Hospitals** - where sick people are treated
- **Shops and malls** - where we buy things
- **Bridges** - to cross rivers and valleys
- **Dams** - to store water and generate electricity

### Roads and Transport:
- **Roads and highways** - for cars and buses
- **Railway tracks** - for trains
- **Airports** - for airplanes
- **Ports** - for ships

### Utilities:
- **Electric poles and wires** - for electricity
- **Water pipes** - to bring water to homes
- **Phone towers** - for communication

## Natural vs Man-made Comparison:

| Natural | Man-made |
|---------|----------|
| River | Canal |
| Cave | Building |
| Forest | Park |
| Lake | Swimming pool |
| Hill | Bridge |
| Sunlight | Electric light |

## The Problem with Too Much Man-made:
- Building **cities** destroys natural areas
- **Factories** can pollute air and water
- **Roads** cut through animal habitats
- **Plastic** and waste harm the environment

## The Solution:
- **Plan carefully** before building
- Use **eco-friendly** materials
- Create **parks and green spaces** in cities
- **Reduce, reuse, recycle**

> **Balance is Key:** We need man-made things for comfortable lives, but we must also protect natural surroundings!

slides.title: Community Spaces
slides.content:
# Community Spaces

**Community spaces** are places shared by everyone in a neighborhood or town. They bring people together!

## Types of Community Spaces:

### Parks and Gardens
- **Public parks** with grass, trees, and benches
- **Playgrounds** with swings, slides, and climbing frames
- **Botanical gardens** with special plants and flowers
- Great for **exercise, relaxation, and family time**

### Educational Spaces
- **Libraries** - free access to books and knowledge
- **Museums** - learn about history, science, and art
- **Community centers** - classes and activities
- **Schools** - learning for children

### Health Spaces
- **Hospitals** and clinics
- **Sports grounds** and stadiums
- **Swimming pools**
- **Walking and jogging tracks**

### Market Spaces
- **Markets** and bazaars
- **Shopping centers**
- **Restaurants** and food courts

### Religious and Cultural Spaces
- **Temples, churches, mosques, gurudwaras**
- **Community halls** for celebrations
- **Cultural centers** for arts and performances

## Rules for Using Community Spaces:
1. Keep them **clean** - do not litter
2. **Share** with others - do not hog space
3. Follow **rules** and guidelines
4. Be **respectful** and quiet when needed
5. Take care of **plants and equipment**
6. Report **damage** to authorities

> **Community Spirit:** When everyone takes care of shared spaces, the whole community benefits. Be a responsible community member!

slides.title: Environmental Awareness
slides.content:
# Environmental Awareness

**Environmental awareness** means understanding how our actions affect the world around us and making better choices.

## Problems Facing Our Environment:

### 1. Pollution
- **Air pollution** from vehicles and factories
- **Water pollution** from garbage and chemicals
- **Land pollution** from trash and plastic
- **Noise pollution** from traffic and construction

### 2. Deforestation
- Cutting down **forests** for farming and building
- Animals lose their **homes**
- Less **oxygen** produced
- More **floods** and soil erosion

### 3. Waste Problem
- Too much **garbage** is produced every day
- **Plastic** does not decompose for hundreds of years
- Garbage fills up **landfills** and pollutes oceans

### 4. Water Scarcity
- Fresh water is becoming **scarce**
- Wasteful use of water
- Pollution of water sources

## What Can YOU Do?

### The 3 R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle!

| Action | Example |
|--------|----------|
| **Reduce** | Use less plastic, save electricity and water |
| **Reuse** | Use cloth bags instead of plastic, refill water bottles |
| **Recycle** | Separate waste, recycle paper and plastic |

### More Actions:
- **Plant trees** whenever you can
- **Walk or cycle** short distances
- **Turn off** lights and fans when not in use
- **Save water** by closing taps properly
- **Spread awareness** - tell friends and family

> **You Have the Power!** Even small actions can make a big difference. Start today and inspire others to join you!

slides.title: Protecting Our Surroundings
slides.content:
# How to Protect Our Surroundings

Protecting our surroundings is everyone's responsibility - including yours!

## At Home:
- **Save electricity** - turn off lights and fans when leaving a room
- **Save water** - turn off taps, take shorter showers
- **Reduce waste** - use less plastic, reuse containers
- **Grow plants** - even small pots make a difference
- **Compost** kitchen waste to make natural fertilizer

## At School:
- Start or join an **Eco Club**
- Organize **clean-up drives**
- Plant trees on **special occasions**
- Make **posters** about saving the environment
- Use both sides of **paper**

## In Your Community:
- Participate in **neighborhood clean-ups**
- Do not throw garbage in **rivers or ponds**
- Support **local farmers** and markets
- Report **pollution** to authorities
- Celebrate **Earth Day** (April 22) and **World Environment Day** (June 5)

## Special Days for the Environment:

| Day | Date | Purpose |
|-----|------|---------|
| Earth Day | April 22 | Celebrate and protect Earth |
| World Environment Day | June 5 | Raise environmental awareness |
| World Water Day | March 22 | Focus on clean water |
| Van Mahotsav | July 1-7 | Plant trees (India) |
| Ozone Day | September 16 | Protect the ozone layer |

> **Promise to Yourself:** I will do at least ONE thing every day to protect my surroundings!

slides.title: Urban vs Rural Surroundings
slides.content:
# Urban vs Rural Surroundings

People live in different types of surroundings. Let's compare **urban (city)** and **rural (village)** areas.

## Urban (City) Surroundings:

### Features:
- Many **tall buildings** and apartments
- Busy **roads** with lots of traffic
- **Schools, hospitals, malls** nearby
- Less **green spaces**
- More **pollution** (air, noise)

### Advantages:
- Better **education** and healthcare
- More **job opportunities**
- Entertainment and **shopping** options
- Good **transport** connections

### Disadvantages:
- **Pollution** and noise
- **Crowded** spaces
- Less connection with **nature**
- **Stressful** lifestyle

## Rural (Village) Surroundings:

### Features:
- **Open fields** and farms
- Lots of **trees** and greenery
- **Fresh air** and clean water
- Fewer buildings and people
- **Animals** and nature everywhere

### Advantages:
- **Clean environment**
- **Fresh food** from farms
- Peaceful and **calm** lifestyle
- Strong **community** bonds

### Disadvantages:
- Fewer **schools** and hospitals
- Less **transport** options
- Fewer **job** opportunities
- Limited **technology** access

## Comparison:

| Feature | Urban | Rural |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Air quality | Polluted | Clean |
| Green spaces | Less | More |
| Facilities | Many | Few |
| Noise | Loud | Quiet |
| Community | Less close | Very close |

> **Both Are Important:** Whether you live in a city or village, take care of your surroundings!

slides.title: Living Things in Our Surroundings
slides.content:
# Living Things in Our Surroundings

Our surroundings are full of living things, even in unexpected places!

## In Your Home:
- **Indoor plants** that purify air
- **Pets** like dogs, cats, fish
- Tiny **ants** in the kitchen
- **Spiders** in corners (they eat mosquitoes!)
- **Mosquitoes** and flies (unwanted visitors)
- **Bacteria and germs** (invisible but present)

## In Your Garden:
- **Butterflies** visiting flowers
- **Earthworms** in the soil (very helpful!)
- **Birds** like sparrows and crows
- **Squirrels** running up trees
- **Bees** pollinating flowers
- Various **plants** and flowers

## In Your Neighborhood:
- **Stray dogs and cats**
- **Crows and pigeons**
- **Trees** lining the roads
- **Grass** and weeds in empty lots

## Helpful vs Harmful Creatures:

| Helpful | Why | Harmful | Why |
|---------|-----|---------|-----|
| Earthworms | Improve soil | Mosquitoes | Spread diseases |
| Bees | Pollinate flowers | Flies | Carry germs |
| Spiders | Eat insects | Cockroaches | Contaminate food |
| Birds | Eat pests | Rats | Damage crops and food |

## How to Attract Helpful Creatures:
- Plant **flowers** to attract butterflies and bees
- Put out **bird feeders** and water bowls
- Avoid **pesticides** that kill helpful insects
- Create a small **compost** area for earthworms

> **Every Creature Has a Purpose:** Even the ones we find annoying play a role in nature's balance!

slides.title: Summary and Key Points
slides.content:
# Summary: Our Surroundings

## Key Concepts:

### Types of Surroundings:
- **Natural** - made by nature (trees, rivers, mountains)
- **Man-made** - created by humans (buildings, roads, bridges)

### Important Environments:
| Environment | Key Features |
|-------------|-------------|
| Home | Clean, organized, ventilated |
| School | Learning spaces, playground, library |
| Community | Parks, markets, hospitals |
| Natural areas | Forests, rivers, mountains |

### Environmental Problems:
- Pollution (air, water, land, noise)
- Deforestation
- Waste and plastic
- Water scarcity

### Solutions - The 3 R's:
1. **Reduce** - Use less
2. **Reuse** - Use again
3. **Recycle** - Transform into new things

### Your Responsibilities:
- Keep home and school **clean**
- **Save** water and electricity
- **Plant trees** and care for plants
- **Do not litter** or pollute
- **Spread awareness** about environmental protection

### Urban vs Rural:
- Cities have more **facilities** but more **pollution**
- Villages have **cleaner air** but fewer services

> **Final Message:** Our surroundings shape who we are. By taking care of them, we take care of ourselves and future generations. Be a **Green Champion** starting today!
